baseline_facts.content: Patient's name is Robert.
Patient is 48 years old.
Patient lives alone.
Patient is a software engineer.
Patient does not smoke.
Patient drinks alcohol infrequently, socially.
Patient has had diarrhea for the past three days.
Patient passes stools 5 to 6 times a day.
Patient's stools are watery and loose.
No visible blood in stools reported.
Vomiting occurred a couple of times at symptom onset.
Vomiting has stopped.
Patient denies abdominal pain.
Patient feels very dehydrated.
Patient has reduced appetite.
Patient has eaten only a little solid food.
Patient felt a bit of temperature at the beginning of illness.
Patient feels very weak.
Patient denies headaches.
Patient denies muscle pains.
Symptoms began at home while working on a computer.
Patient does not recall recent takeaway or restaurant food.
No known contact with someone with diarrhea in the last week.
Patient has taken time off work for the last three days due to feeling unwell.
Patient has asthma.
Patient uses a blue inhaler infrequently.
Patient takes no other regular medications.
No known drug allergies.
Patient's father had high blood pressure.
Patient's father died of bowel cancer about ten years ago.
Patient's mother has type 2 diabetes.
Doctor suspects gastroenteritis.
Patient was advised to drink plenty of fluids.
Patient was advised to use Dioralyte for fluid replacement.
Patient may take Paracetamol if feeling feverish and weak.
Patient was advised to continue time off work for the next day or two.
Patient was advised to be diarrhea-free for about 24 to 48 hours before returning to work.
Patient was advised to return next week if not better.

candidate_facts.content: Chief complaint of diarrhea for approximately 3 days.
Patient felt warm or possibly febrile at the beginning of illness.
Symptoms began at home while working on a computer.
Patient uses a “blue inhaler” for asthma.
Inhaler use is infrequent and as needed.
Father died of colorectal cancer approximately 10 years ago.
Off work for the past 3 days due to illness.
Illness is most consistent with viral gastroenteritis.
Foodborne toxin-mediated illness is considered possible.
Oral rehydration solution use was advised.
Frequent small sips of fluids were advised.
Paracetamol as needed for feverish feeling or aches was advised.
Continue time off work for the next 1–2 days until improved was advised.
Return to work after being diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours was advised.
Reassessment next week if not improved was advised.
Continue current inhaler use as needed was advised.
Patient is able to take some fluids.
A few episodes of vomiting occurred at symptom onset.
